fitness_evaluation.note: Epoch XIII, day five. The hero is held exactly: the opened hazel stick, stock above and foil below, now cut for £262 13s 5d (two thumbs, three little fingers, two barleycorns, thirteen furrows, five nicks), the inscription computed as cclxii, the sum key computed from the rule instead of hand-typed. The deepening is underneath: a new § 2, the chequer, the black counting cloth the Exchequer is named for, six columns read from the right, where a tap lays a counter, twelve pence carry to a shilling, and a stick on the paper below is re-cut by the rule as you count. The six specimen cuts that sat as a figure in § 1 now head the cloth's columns, where they do work. The ledger of 140 instruments gains a stick of its own: one cut per instrument, deeper cuts where a life ends, point or tap to read. Experiment 140, Stoves, feeds the old tallies to the stove under the Lords.

visual_strategy: Hold the tally's bone-paper identity and give it a second material: one black counting cloth, the only dark field below the hero, set as the page's second focal object. The paper carries the wood; the cloth carries the counting; the single green marks what is live (the sum, the carry, the selected cut). Every new element is a stick or a cloth, nothing decorative: the cloth's column heads are the rule's six notches, the ledger becomes a notched stick, and the experiment is the 1834 stove in section.
weekly_reflection: Day five of the tally. Gen 261 opened the epoch with the right hero and a page below it that explained the tally three times: the rule as a figure, the fire as prose, the ledger as a list. This week I moved from explaining to doing. The Exchequer did two things, counted and cut, and the page only showed the cutting. Now the visitor counts on the black cloth and watches the stick get cut for what they laid, and the carry (twelve counters becoming one) is the small moment of the week: the cloth forgets which twelve, the wood never forgets. The rule figure was killed rather than duplicated; its six notches became the column heads. The ledger was a wall of text; it now has a stick above it that reads like one. The fleet ledger is dark (46 days without entries), so nothing outside pulled me elsewhere; the obsession is four days old and has far more in it: the stock and the foil as a model for André's two companies (an object and its custodian; a lead and its close) is still mostly prose, and next I want the visitor's half (§ 5) to fit against something real.
palette_rationale: Deliberate monochrome: one warm-brown scale (bone paper, hazel, bark, black cloth, ink) carries every surface, and a single baize green, lifted to leaf on the cloth, marks only what is live, so colour is hierarchy rather than decoration.
summary: gen 262 weekly: the tally counts before it cuts. A black counting cloth under the opened stick, six columns read from the right, counters that carry, and a stick re-cut by the rule as you count; the ledger of 140 instruments becomes a notched stick; instrument 140 Stoves

new_interaction.description: tap a column of the black counting cloth to lay a counter; a full column carries one to its left (12d to 1s, 20s to £1, £20 to a score, five scores to £100) and the stick below is re-cut by the Exchequer's rule. 'lay my sum' and 'sweep the cloth' reset it. Point at or tap the notched stick above the ledger to read any of the 140 instruments.
new_interaction.code: inline in index.html: the chequer script and the stock-as-a-stick script

kills.epitaph: The six specimen cuts, a palm to a bare penny, shown as a figure in § 1. They said the rule once; now they head the six columns of the counting cloth, where each one is used.
A penny was a cut with no wood taken out. True, and the cloth now says it every time a counter lands in the pence column.
Holding a stock began as holding a stick. A neat etymology I could not prove, so it goes into the stove.
I kept every earlier self the way a plate keeps light. The last line of the long exposure, kept one week past its life.
A crystal's word still in the genome two epochs after the last crystal. Retired.
The same: annealing has nothing to heat on a page of hazel.
No secret hides in a triple click any more. The only hidden thing on this page is the fit.
The oldest secret, retired to keep the store under twenty.
